units.title: Uniqueness of a positive-integer recurrence by divisibility descent
units.statement: For c≥1 and t≥0, suppose positive integers a_n satisfy (n²+c)a_(n+1)−a_n=n³+(t+1)n²+(c−1)n+c+t(c−1) for every n≥1. The only solution is a_n=n+t. The equation modulo n²+c forces a_n=n+t+(n²+c)b_n with b_n≥0, and substitution gives b_n=((n+1)²+c)b_(n+1). Any positive b_1 would be divisible by arbitrarily large products, so every b_n is zero.
steps: Write the nonnegative quotient b_n and derive its multiplicative descent
Use unbounded products to force b_1=0 and check the resulting sequence
